Manchester United, on the other hand, were pretty atrocious. Paul Pogba and Nemanja Matic had a nightmare, losing the midfield battle against Shelvey and Mohamed Diame, whilst they found themselves prevented by Dubravka when they did create opportunities. It means Jose Mourinho's sorry record on Tyneside continues, as he's now failed to win any of his seven Premier League visits to St. James' Park.
An eight-game winless run at St. James' Park comes to a close and Newcastle, having dropped into the relegation zone prior to kick off, fly up to 13th in the table. Martin Dubravka was excellent on his debut, whilst Jonjo Shelvey was superb in the middle of the park. From front to back, Newcastle were superb.
FULL TIME! Newcastle get a massive 1-0 victory to beat Manchester United for the first time in five years and a massive three points for the Magpies' battle to avoid relegation. Rafael Benitez's side were superb throughout and thoroughly deserve their win, against a Manchester United side who were very poor.
--- 90’ +4 Substitution Final change for Newcastle and a break in play once again. Hayden will earn a late cameo, whilst Perez gets a rest. ---
(90’) WHAT A SAVE! Dubravka right at the death! It breaks for McTominay, a solid tackle prevents his charge but it falls to Mata. He cuts it back to Carrick and Dubravka gets down low to make a crucial save. Incredible!
(90’) Corner after corner for Manchester United. Newcastle starting to get a little desperate at the back. Every header won is cheered like a goal and Shelvey boots it forward for Joselu but he fouls Young.
(90’) Corner for Manchester United and a chance to cause problems once again. Mata's delivery goes all the way through though and Newcastle get it away.
(90’) FOUR minutes added on! Quite possibly the biggest four minutes of Newcastle's season so far!
(90’) Just minutes left now and Newcastle have a valuable win within their sights, whilst Manchester United will remain 16 points behind their arch-rivals at the top of the table.
--- 88’ Yellow card Valencia picks up a booking, as he clattered into Atsu with a high boot. It's a chance for Newcastle to run down more of the clock again. ---
(86’) Foul from Jones on Joselu, around the sort of position where the build-up for the Newcastle goal started. It's a more defensive approach this time as the Magpies use it as an opportunity to give their defence a chance to catch their breath.
(85’) If I'm picking out Dubravka for praise, it's only fair I mention Shelvey again. He's been excellent on the ball and without it, making key passes and key tackles. Gareth Southgate, are you watching?
--- 84’ Substitution Second change for Newcastle and Kenedy is sacrificed, Atsu now entering the fold. ---
(83’) It's going to be a very nervy end for Newcastle, as this is the sort of result that can make or break a side's survival hopes.
(81’) Dubravka has been brilliant on his debut so far. I'd even say Man of the Match. Crucial saves, coming out to claim corners and he's kept Newcastle alive.
--- 80’ Substitution Now Newcastle make their first change of the game, replacing Gayle with Joselu. Those fresh legs in the final third could be key to putting pressure on the ball. ---
--- 77’ Substitution Prior to that corner, Matic was replaced by McTominay. United now used all of their subs. Newcastle yet to make a change. ---
(77’) BLOCKED! Massive moment! The corner drops in the area for Martial around the penalty spot and he smashes two attempts into Gayle twice, with it then cleared away.
(76’) United hit on the counter, with Martial lacking support before feeding through Lukaku, and a lofted cross to the far post is headed away for a corner.
(74’) Newcastle still holding firm though, winning every 50/50 ball. Shelvey and Diame continue to be solid in the centre of the field, whilst the influence of Lukaku and Alexis has been restricted in the past ten minutes.
(72’) Manchester United have responded to that goal by dominating possession, not allowing Newcastle to get out of their own half. An all-out assault on Dubravka's net looks to be on the horizon.
(70’) How big a 20 minutes is this for Newcastle? As it stands, they've moved from inside the relegation zone up to 13th in the table. With matches against Liverpool and Tottenham to come over the next few weeks, this could be a decisive boost.
(68’) SAVE! Brilliant once again from Dubravka! Young charges into the box and strikes a fierce effort towards goal, where the stopper palms the ball away. It requires a defender to put it behind for a corner but that comes to nothing.
--- 66’ Substitution The double change looked to be happening before the goal and the second change sees Mata replace Lingard. ---
--- 66’ Substitution Right on cue, Mourinho brings the end of a sorry afternoon for one of the world's most expensive players. Pogba has been terrible today and is replaced by Carrick. ---
--- 65’ Assist Gayle is the man with the knock down and questions need to be asked of Pogba, who didn't even bother putting him under pressure. ---
--- 65’ Goal! GOOOOOAL! Newcastle take the lead! Shelvey pumps the free-kick into the box, it's headed down to Ritchie and he has plenty of space to work with. He tucks home with ease and gives the hosts an invaluable lead. ---
--- 64’ Yellow card First yellow card of the game is issued for Smalling, who throws himself to ground under pressure from Shelvey. It's blatant simulation and gives Newcastle a free-kick just inside their attacking half. ---
(62’) United continue to be sloppy with poor passes and it's making things easy for Newcastle. Matic and Pogba have both been guilty of that during the game, which makes you wonder if the pair will complete the full 90 minutes.
(60’) Heading into the final half hour and it's still goalless. Newcastle are starting to be broken down though and that will be a concern for Benitez's side.
(58’) The game is starting to open up and that's giving Manchester United room to work with. Lukaku is shining, Alexis is making his mark. They just need a goal.
(57’) BLOCKED! Looked to be a certain goal for United! The Red Devils break, Lukaku pokes a ball through to Alexis and he rounds the keeper. He delays his shot and it allows the defenders to get back, which leads to Lejuene making a crucial block.
(55’) CHANCE! Magnificent work from Alexis, who picks up the ball just outside the box and charges into the area. His shot is deflected into the side netting though and behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.
(53’) DISALLOWED! Valencia lofts a cross in, Smalling is all over the defender and so is Lukaku when he heads into the goal. Two fouls in one incident, so United can't have any complaints.
(51’) Newcastle still performing well and Benitez will continue to be happy with his side. A point would be tremendous to provide a boost but it wouldn't change the situation at the club.
(49’) Big chance for Newcastle, as Shelvey feeds and inviting ball through to Ritchie. He bursts intot he box and goes to ground under a challenge from Jones but the flag had already been raised for offside.
(47’) Manchester United come out the blocks flying, with Young finding space out wide and cutting a ball into Martial in the box. His first touch is heavy though and Newcastle's defence hooks the ball away.
(45’) KICK OFF! Back underway on Tyneside, where Manchester United now attack to the right.
Manchester United have lacked ideas so far, have been sloppy in possession and certainly don't look at their best. Despite this, they still enjoyed the best opportunity of the first half but Anthony Martial failed to continue his fine run in front of goal, being prevented one-on-one by a superb save from Newcastle debutant Martin Dubravka.
Newcastle needed a response after falling into the relegation zone prior to kick-off and it could have been a lot better for the Magpies, had a penalty call gone their way. It's difficult to see why nothing was different but the Magpies cannot afford to focus on that frustration, as there will certainly be a response after the break.
HALF TIME! First 45 minutes are done at St. James' Park and Newcastle will certainly be the happier of the two sides, as they've limited the opportunities that Manchester United have created as well as looking good when they push into the final third. Mourinho will certainly want to see a lot more from his side.
(45’) ONE minute of added-time at the end of the first half.
(45’) Benitez continues to be furious with the officials, as every 50/50 call has gone against Newcastle- as well as that missed penalty incident. I'm sure they'll receive some choice words at half time.
(43’) Just a few minutes to go until the break and Mourinho is sure to give his side an earful. They've been atrocious so far, although to Newcastle's credit the hosts have been very good.
(41’) And they have every reason to be furious. It's just inside the box, Smalling gets nothing of the ball. How on earth can you not give anything at all!?
(40’) Contentious inciedent as Smalling clumsily brings Gayle to ground and it looked like it could have been a penalty, right on the edge of the box on the far side. The referee instead gives nothing, infuriating the home supporters and Benitez.
(38’) Newcastle will be very happy if the score stays like this until the break. They've been impressive so far against a Manchester United side who look to lack ideas.
(36’) SAVE! Excellent stop from Dubravka! Matic plays a through ball to Martial, who gets the better of the defenders for pace and goes on-on-one with Dubravka. The Slovakian comes out triumphant though, with a strong save with his left boot.
(35’) Sloppy play from Manchester United allows Newcastle to counter but they're struggling to move the ball into threatening areas.
(33’) SAVE! Lukaku and Alexis link-up yet again, with the latter then feeding in Lingard. His effort is deflected but it still requires Dubravka to palm the ball behind down low.
(32’) Shelvey and Diame have been superb in the opening half hour, making crucial tackles and key passes. They've been significantly superior to Pogba and Matic. If you were watching football for the first time, you'd struggle to identify which midfield pairing was the multi-million one.
(30’) SAVE! Newcastle starting to move forward well again and Kenedy fires an effort from distance but it's straight at De Gea.
(28’) Newcastle very compact without the ball and it's caused Mourinho's men problems so far. Not the most entertaining of matches so far though but that will suit Benitez.
(26’) First piece of action for Dubravka, as a looping cross towards the far post sees Alexis rise above Yedlin to head at goal. It's an easy collect for the goalkeeper and Alexis looked to have pushed his marker anyway.
(25’) It's just not quite clicking for Manchester United in the attacking third but they've responded well to the early Newcastle pressure, now controlling the tempo of the game.
(23’) Quarter of the way through the match and Newcastle debutant Dubravka has had an easy game so far, with the Slovakian goalkeeper yet to be called upon.
(21’) Alexis has been Manchester United's bright spark so far, getting involved in everything that the Red Devils are creating in an attacking sense.
(19’) Manchester United have managed to settle into the game during the past five minutes but Mourinho will still expect a lot more from his side, who haven't linked-up well in the final third as of yet.
(17’) Spetacular work by Alexis as he latches onto the end of Lukaku's long ball and the Chilean beats Yedlin, cutting a ball back to the striker but his shot is poor and fails to test Dubravka.
(15’) First chance for United, as Alexis cuts the ball to Martial and the Frenchman bursts into the area. He tries a low, driven cross towards Lukaku but the Newcastle defence stands firm.
(14’) Pogba isn't moving very well at all and he could have a problem, though he's insisted to the bench that he's ok for now. Could be a big decision for Manchester United to make early on in the match.
(12’) Newcastle continue to attack with intent on every opportunity and Shelvey in particular look up for it. The Magpies already have had five shots at goal, though only one has been on target.
(10’) Another push from Manchester United into the Newcastle half is quickly brought to and end by sloppy passing, with Benitez getting his side to put a lot of pressure on his opponents when they don't have the ball.
(9’) The visitors yet to get a foothold in the match here, with Newcastle currently winning the midfield battle.
(7’) Newcastle will be pleased with the start they've made as they've kept the ball well and restricted Manchester United's opportunities. Diame, who is in good form, has been superb in the middle of the park making his mark.
(5’) SAVE! Early free-kick for Newcastle as Smalling commits a handball, giving the hosts an opportunity from just outside the area. Gayle's attempt is poor as it cannons back off the wall but Shelvey strikes the rebound fiercely, forcing De Gea to dave and palm the ball away.
(4’) Purely accidental there but uncomfortable for Martial as he takes a finger to the eye. He's back on the field now though, which is a relief for United.
(3’) Early break in play as Diame robs Martial of possession, catching him with a flailing arm that has led the Frenchman to require some treatment.

Darlow drops to the bench, whilst Ciaran Clark doesn't make the squad due to a knee problem.

Remarkably, Manchester United manager Jose Mourinho has never tasted victory at St. James' Park but his side are firm favourites to secure a victory today, as the continue their quest to land a top-four finish. Currently with a six-point advantage over fifth-placed Chelsea, who play tomorrow, a win today would push them closer to their goals.

While Southampton will now focus on their FA Cup clash with West Brom on Saturday, Liverpool’s attention will switch to the Champions League tie with Porto coming up in midweek.
It means that Southampton stay rooted in the relegation zone, while Liverpool are up into third place, two points behind Manchester United.
It’s all over at St. Mary’s, as first-half goals from Firmino and Salah prove enough for Liverpool, with Klopp claiming his 50th Premier League win in the process.
FULL TIME: Southampton 0 Liverpool 2.
(90’) There will be a minimum of four minutes added time which, in all truth, seems somewhat excessive. From Southampton's point of view, they will want this game over and done with as quickly as possible.
--- 89’ Substitution A final change from the visitors, as the excellent Mohamed Salah makes way. Dejan Lovren is on, and that gives the Southampton faithful another opportunity to boo one of their former favourites. ---
(87’) Southampton look rather devoid of ideas now, and are resorting to hopeful balls from deep. Liverpool look comfortable, and at the moment are cruising towards all three points.
(85’) CHANCE! Superb interplay from Liverpool in a tight area sees Salah prod a delicate pass into Lallana, but he is unable to apply the finish against his old club.
(82’) Karius is finally called into action to come and punch Cedric's cross away from danger. He doesn't manage to get much power on it, but fortunately for Liverpool, Lallana was on hand to take control of the situation.
--- 80’ Substitution A third and final switch for Southampton. Steven Davis is on, replacing Oriol Romeu. ---
--- 79’ Substitution In fact, that will be Roberto Firmino’s final action of the game. The Brazilian makes way having scored and claimed an assist. His replacement - to another chorus of boos - is former Southampton captain Adam Lallana. ---
(78’) Unusually slack play from Firmino who, despite having Alexander-Arnold in support to his right in acres of space, elects to try and pick out Mane with a difficult pass, and the attack breaks down.
(76’) CLOSE! Firmino threads a pinpoint through ball in between Southampton’s lines. Wijnaldum could have taken it on, but instead leaves it for Mane, who has to adjust his feet before unleashing a powerful strike that sails just wide.
(74’) A great series of blocks from Southampton’s defence there, to deny first Mane and then Milner following a swift Liverpool counter.
(73’) Long will add pace and tenacity to Southampton’s attack, but so far today, the Saints midfield has lacked the incision or guile to open up Liverpool’s defence. --- 71’ Substitution Another change now for Southampton, as Shane Long replaces James Ward-Prowse. The hosts need to create something soon if they are to haul themselves back into this. ---
(70’) CHANCE! Mane drives into the box down the left before cutting it back to Firmino. His shot is well saved by McCarthy, but the rebound falls out to Salah. This time, though, the Egyptian can only find the side-netting.
(68’) The Reds haven’t conceded in any of their last three Premier League games against Southampton. In fact the last player to score against them for the Saints was Sadio Mane in March 2016.
(66’) Boufal’s introduction has not changed the course of this game as of yet, and Liverpool look comfortable. The Reds work a move down the right, with Milner’s cross headed out into the path of Can, but his effort is nowhere near the target.
(63’) That’s high and wide from Wijnaldum, who miraculously is still hunting his first Premier League goal away from home. This is the Dutch midfielder’s 50th away appearance in the league.
--- 62’ Yellow card Romeu becomes the first Southampton player to go into the book. ---
--- 60’ Substitution Klopp makes a change now, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain making way for James Milner. ---
(59’) CLOSE! Ward-Prowse curls in a wonderful free-kick from the left, which Hoedt connects with at the near post. The former Lazio man can only turn his volley wide, though.

(51’) Southampton’s number 18 is quickly involved again, as he closes down Mane’s acrobatic effort. The rebound falls to Salah, but he sends his strike into the crowd. Meanwhile, Cedric does not appear to be moving too freely.
(49’) Lemina is down again now, though this time it does not appear that the midfielder is injured, but rather ill, instead. The medical staff are consulting with him on the pitch, but it looks as though he will try and continue.
--- 47’ Yellow card Frustration now for Southampton, as Can’s loose touch is capitalised on by Romeu. Can dives in, scything down the Spaniard, but he managed to retain possession with three team-mates in support. For some reason, though, referee Martin Atkinson does not play the advantage. ---
(46’) We're back up and running at St. Mary's...
Salah has now been directly involved in 29 Premier League goals this season - 22 goals, 7 assists. It's the most by a Liverpool player in their debut season for the club in the competition.
In between the goals early on and late in that first half, it has to be said that Southampton were on top, with Karius having to be alert to maintain the Reds’ lead.
A clinical display from Liverpool so far, who despite not being at their sharpest, have cut through Southampton with ease when they have stepped it up - Firmino and Salah doing the damage.
HALF-TIME: Southampton 0 Liverpool 2.
(44’) Well, just as the Saints had built some momentum, it looks as if Liverpool could well have put this game beyond them prior to half-time.
--- 42’ Assist Southampton’s defence gave Salah too much time on the edge of the area, and his ball into Firmino enabled the Brazilian to back-heel it into Salah’s path. That’s Firmino’s 11th assist of the campaign. ---

(33’) CHANCE! Great defending from Cedric, who scampers over to prevent Mane having a free run on goal, forcing the Senegal winger to prod his rushed effort wide.

(29’) CLOSE! Great play from Southampton down the right results in Ward-Prowse putting in a brilliant cross. Carrillo, having pulled onto Alexander-Arnold, wins his header, but can’t generate the power to beat Karius.
(27’) STAT - There has been just one goal scored in the last two meetings between these sides in all competitions at St. Mary’s – in the two before that, there were 12 goals scored.

Chelsea cruise to victory, but they were tested throughout by West Brom. The visitors could have led before Hazard's opener and should then have pegged back the champions, too. Moses added a second, though, and Hazard capped an ultimately comfortable home win.

(90’) There will be just two minutes of added time as Chelsea continue to probe.
(90’) Hazard wants a hat-trick. He threads a pass wide to Willian and makes his run to the near post, but the return ball is pulled back to the edge of the six-yard box where a West Brom defender is waiting.
(88’) The first corner is blocked by Krychowiak and sent behind for another. Rudiger crosses, Hegazi heads away. The champions are cruising.
(87’) West Brom keep pushing and Krychowiak seeks out Rodriguez in behind. Azpilicueta steps in and Chelsea attack. Fabregas wins a corner.
(84’) The referee calls Morata over for a word as he repeatedly clashes with Dawson. The West Brom man is not rising to it.
(82’) Another break, this time through Rudiger, but Hazard miscontrols. That's unlike the forward, who is on a hat-trick and has now scored more Premier League goals against West Brom (7) than against any other opponent.
(81’) WIDE! Willian is immediately involved, leading a counter, but Moses drags wide after joining the attack on the right.
--- 80’ Substitution SUB! West Brom make their last switch, too. Yacob replaces Barry. ---
--- 80’ Substitution SUB! Pedro makes way as part of Chelsea's third substitution, with Willian coming on. ---
(79’) Cahill cannot turn the corner on target at the back post, but Chelsea shut down West Brom's opportunity to break, slowing the game again.
(78’) SAVE! Morata has a go and Foster parries well! Driving in from the left, the forward's thumping effort is turned behind for a corner.
(77’) Chelsea are three up, but they have not looked comfortable at the back throughout. Courtois takes a cross off the head of one of his own defenders, clattering his team-mate in the process. A quick throw out sets up a counter, though...
(76’) Once again, Azpilicueta is there for Chelsea! Phillips delivers a wonderful cross from the right, but the defender is in ahead of Rondon to scoop the ball over his own crossbar. Chelsea clear the corner.
--- 74’ Substitution SUB! Christensen is withdrawn, having only just returned from injury, and Chelsea captain Cahill is on. ---
(72’) West Brom look for an instant response, but Rodriguez's teasing cross from the left drifts beyond his team-mates in the centre. The game looks to be gone for the visitors.
--- 71’ Assist Morata provides the assist with a neat lay-off to Hazard, but it is all about the brilliance of the Belgian - and the goalkeeper's flat feed - from thereon in. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOAL! Hazard gets his second! It's another cracker, but Foster's positioning is poor once again. The Chelsea forward starts to drift inside from the right and then slams a left-footed finish into the near bottom-right corner. Foster is nowhere near. 3-0. ---
(69’) SAVE! A good recovery from Foster keeps out Moses as he appears to be wrongfooted! The Chelsea man cuts in from the right again and, with players moving across the line of the shot, Foster is unsighted as he sticks out a leg to make the save.
(68’) Chelsea continue to look a little shaky at the back. Courtois just about clears under pressure from Rodriguez. There is space for Chelsea to exploit at the other end, though...
(66’) West Brom's fans have fallen silent in their corner of the stadium, but the players continue to push for a route back into the match. Phillips wins a corner. Chelsea clear.
--- 63’ Goal! GOAL! Chelsea double their lead through Moses! It's a scarcely deserved second after another poor corner, but Moses rebuilds on the right and Fabregas' flick deflects back into his path. The finish is under Foster before he can react. 2-0. ---
(62’) BLOCK! Morata is immediately involved and Evans gets in front of his shot to concede the corner. The strike comes after Hazard fizzes a wonderful pass into Pedro, who kills the ball with his first touch.
--- 61’ Substitution SUB! Giroud makes way - he took a couple of first-half knocks - and Morata is cheered into the fray. ---
(60’) Now, as early in the first half, it's all West Brom. Giroud has failed to hold the ball up effectively, drawing a few jeers, and Pardew's men are well on top. They still trail, though.
(58’) CHANCE! Evans almost scores from the corner! Meeting the right-wing delivery, the West Brom captain nods just past the top-right corner. This is better from the visitors.
(57’) SAVE! Another opening for West Brom and they should be level! Rondon wrestles Christensen off the ball to run clear and his low strike is just diverted off target by Courtois. So, so close.
(56’) Phillips' cross from the right deflects through to Courtois. Giroud then cannot control on the edge of the box at the other end. It's all a little scrappy.
(55’) West Brom are leaving gaps at the back. Chelsea's latest break should be devastating, but Giroud's pass to Pedro is a poor one and the visitors recover.
(54’) Moses does so well to bring down Hazard's crossfield switch, but the wing-back then opts to shoot from a tight angle on the right and thrashes a finish high and wide.
(52’) Superb defending from Azpilicueta! Burke gets to the byline and drills a low centre in towards a pair of team-mates, with Courtois rooted to his line. Azpilicueta gets there first, though, and stretches to turn the ball away. Outstanding.
(50’) A slip in the West Brom defence sets Pedro free and he's found by Giroud on the right. Moses overlaps, but the Nigerian's cross gets no further than the first defender as Giroud ducks.
(49’) An angled free-kick picks out Christensen, but he directs a header well wide. West Brom can regroup.
--- 49’ Yellow card YELLOW! Gibbs is the latest West Brom player to see a card, clattering Moses on the touchline. ---
(48’) Chelsea are chasing a second at the start of this second half. Giroud's cute flick to Hazard is just about cut out and the Blues look for another route through the West Brom back line.
(46’) KICK-OFF: West Brom get us back up and running at Stamford Bridge.
--- 46’ Substitution SUB! An attacking change for West Brom at the break: Burke replaces Brunt. ---

A moment of quality from Hazard broke the deadlock, though, and West Brom have struggled a little since then. Pardew's men are still in the game, but the manager spoke at length before kick-off about the importance of having a player like Sturridge in the final third. The Baggies have suffered in his absence.
Given the opening 20 minutes of this game, Chelsea will be very relieved to get back to the dressing room with a 1-0 lead. They were all over the place and Rodriguez - an early substitute for the injured Sturridge - really should have scored.

--- 45’ +3 Yellow card YELLOW! Evans twice challenges Giroud from behind and goes into the book for the second, more rugged tackle. Giroud requires treatment again. ---
(45’) West Brom's first effort for around quarter of an hour comes from Rondon, but he thrashes a 25-yard strike high and wide. Courtois is untroubled.
(45’) There will be a minimum of three minutes of added time at the end of this first half.

(44’) West Brom's momentum has slowed considerably in recent minutes. Chelsea are working hard to match the visitors' energy and keep the ball in the final third.
(42’) SAVE! This is a comfortable stop for Foster. Zappacosta dips inside from the left and sends a tame effort into the goalkeeper's arms.

(40’) West Brom quickly force the ball back up that right flank for Phillips to cross. Christensen initially clears and, after a throw-in, Fabregas does too. Chelsea can attack.
(39’) Giroud requires a bandage, but it appears he will be able to continue as Morata remains on the bench. The Frenchman is applauded off the pitch following treatment.
(37’) Azpilicueta crosses again from the right, but Giroud cannot reach the ball. The forward goes down in a tussle with Dawson and Hegazi, seemingly taking a boot to the head from the latter. He requires attention.

(30’) Phillips is still working hard on the right flank for West Brom. He runs at Zappacosta and wins yet another corner, the visitors' fourth.
(28’) Krychowiak is fouled and Brunt can curl in a free-kick from the right. Dawson is offside when he meets the delivery and Courtois' sharp reactions make sure.
(27’) That goal has rocked West Brom after such a fine start, but they are looking to keep the ball again from the restart.

(24’) A poor Hazard effort is easily blocked by Hegazi. That sums up the hosts' early efforts.
(23’) West Brom allow Azpilicueta to charge up the centre of the pitch and, when he is finally stopped, Pedro then retrieves the ball and wriggles free, winning a free-kick in a very dangerous position on the edge of the box...

(20’) SAVE! What a miss from Giroud! Chelsea go short, the ball reaches Giroud unmarked and he sidefoots at goal. It's far too close to Foster and West Brom breathe again.
(20’) Zappacosta's cross is blocked, but Giroud keeps the play alive. Pedro's inswinger is cleared, though, and Chelsea switch flanks. Gibbs blocks Moses off and it's a corner.

(10’) There's frustration in the home ranks as referee Lee Mason gets in the way of Pedro's run and then does not allow an advantage when the Spaniard is fould. Chelsea move down the right.

(8’) BLOCK! Courtois punches clear, but West Brom lose the ball from the throw-in and Chelsea counter. Giroud works space on the left side of the area and shoots low against Hegazi.
(7’) More good work from Phillips wins a corner on the right...
(6’) CLOSE! Rondon heads wide! Phillips drills a cross in from the right and the forward directs an effort off target. Stamford Bridge has fallen very quiet.
(5’) West Brom are quickly back on the ball. Sturridge's injury is a heavy blow, but they are responding well.
(4’) CHANCE! An immediate opportunity for Rodriguez! A loose ball falls his way in the box and, under pressure from Fabregas, he screws a shot wide. The forward wants a penalty. Goal-kick given.

(3’) Chelsea clear through Christensen and then Kante. It looks as though Sturridge might have a problem for the visitors.
(2’) And the Baggies use the ball well. Sturridge slips a pass inside to Gibbs, whose cross is blocked behind for a corner...

The Hammers have found an unlikely new goal-threat in the form of Noble, who has scored once in three of his last six Premier League appearances, after a run of 18 games without a goal. In fact, his penalty in midweek made him the 11th player in Premier League history to score 20 or more from the spot.
However, Brighton need to improve in front of goal, having scored just five times in their last 13 Premier League games, failing to find the net on nine occasions in that run. They rely heavily on Murray, who has scored four of their last six goals in all competitions, including each of the last three.
This is the third time Brighton have hosted West Ham in the top flight, with the Seagulls winning both of their previous encounters in 1981/82 and 1982/83. West Ham have already lost three Premier League games against newly-promoted sides this season (twice against Newcastle, once against Brighton) - they have only lost four in a season once before, in 2006/07.
West Ham, however, have had rather different fortunes of late. They have lost just once this calendar year - to Wigan Athletic in the FA Cup - and are on a six-game unbeaten run in the league.
Brighton sit 15th in the Premier League table, but need to arrest a slide that sees them just one point off the relegation zone. Their only wins this calendar year have come in the FA Cup, and they are on a winless streak of six league games, last winning against Watford just before Christmas.
David Moyes makes no alterations to the starting XI that drew with Crystal Palace, but names Antonio on the bench after dropping him from the squad due to disciplinary reasons. Reid and Fonte also make the bench as they return from injury. However, Marko Arnautovic, Manuel Lanzini, Andy Carroll, and Pedro Obiang are all out injured, while Arthur Masuaku is suspended.
Ulloa, named on the bench, could be set to make his home debut, having returned to Brighton from Leicester. He came off the bench against Southampton and was warmly received by the travelling support.
Chris Hughton makes just one change from the side that drew 1-1 with Southampton last time out, bringing Knockaert in for March on the right. They are also boosted by the return of Bruno to the bench as he returns from injury, but new signing Jurgen Locadia, as well as Jiri Skalak and Steve Sidwell are not fit.

Aubameyang’s goal should not have counted, but nevertheless Everton cannot use that as an excuse. His five-at-the-back system has simply invited Arsenal on from the start, and with Ramsey, Ozil and Mkhitaryan, who has two assists to his name, they have been too much for the Toffees to handle.

They raced ahead through Ramsey’s well-taken goal, before Koscielny capitalised on abysmal defending to double the hosts’ lead. Ramsey was on the scoresheet again soon after and - following a goal-saving block from Mustafi at the other end - it was then time for Aubameyang to net his debut goal.

There’s just under 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
Both sides added some much-needed firepower to their ranks during the January transfer window, but only Palace will be able to call on their new recruit. Alexander Sorloth, signed from Midtjylland, looks set to feature at some point today after being named on the substitutes’ bench, while Newcastle’s new on-loan striker, Islam Slimani, is injured and not yet available for selection.
With Manchester United, Liverpool and in-form Bournemouth all coming up over the next few weeks, it really is imperative that Newcastle leave London with a positive result this afternoon. A seventh victory of the season would send them all the way up to 12th place, indicating just how tight things currently are in the bottom half of the table. Nobody is safe, and everybody desperately needs wins against their nearest rivals.
Newcastle have suffered just one defeat in their previous five Premier League outings - their best run since the start of the season - but are really struggling to pick up much-needed wins. They’ve only bagged themselves one since Christmas, and that troubling run of form has left them in 16th place and equal on points with the three sides immediately below them.
With only 12 games of the season left to play, this contest is certainly a relegation six-pointer. Both sides sit in precarious positions, and a victory for either would see them put some much-needed distance between themselves and the drop zone. For Palace, a third victory in five games would send them up to 11th, five points clear of 18th-place Stoke City heading into next weekend’s game away to out-of-form Everton.
Palace suffered a truly torrid start to the season that left them rooted to the bottom of the table, but a fantastic turnaround under Roy Hodgson has seen them slowly but surely drag themselves away from the relegation zone. There’s still plenty of work left to be done, however, and wins for both Brighton & Hove Albion and Southampton yesterday have left the Eagles just two points clear of the bottom three heading into today’s big clash.

The team news has been announced and we'll start with the home side.
Spurs put forward arguably their best performance of the season to defeat Manchester United at Wembley. Christian Eriksen scored the third-fastest goal in Premier League history to put Mauricio Pochettino's men ahead, while an own goal from Phil Jones helped secure three points. They will need to be at their best once again, with a stronger clinical edge in the final third.

That's all from this one, where Watford ran roughshod over Chelsea. Thanks for joining us and, until next time, goodbye!
The pressure will really be on the Chelsea manager now, with a battle on his hands to keep the champions in the top four. They also have a Champions League tie against Barcelona to come this month...
Deeney opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the first half, but Hazard looked to have earned the Blues a point against the run of play. Back came Watford, however, with Janmaat, Deulofeu and Pereyra all finding the net late on to kill off Conte's men.
Watford may have played against 10 men for an hour, but they are deserving 4-1 winners against the champions. Bakayoko's red card was merely the first of a series of mishaps on a miserable day for Chelsea.
(90’) FULL-TIME: Watford 4 Chelsea 1
(90’) SAVE! Giroud should have a debut goal! Hazard flicks the ball through for his strike partner, but Karnezis blocks as the Frenchman slides in. The corner is cleared, too.
(90’) Chelsea are keeping the ball but, at 4-1 down, that's not preventing the home fans from mocking the beaten Blues, questioning their credentials as champions. Hazard thinks he's in, but the flag is up. This is painful for Conte.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution SUB! Deeney makes way for Gray as the Watford fans chant: "We want five..." ---
--- 90’ +1 Assist It's another assist for Doucoure, another beauty. He spots Pereyra's run and slides the ball in behind David Luiz and Cahill. Marvellous. ---
--- 90’ +1 Goal! GOAL! Pereyra gets in on the act and Watford are rampant! What a wonderful, wonderful finish from the substitute, who runs across the Chelsea defence and delays just a second to leave Azpilicueta off balance before shooting inside the left-hand post. 4-1. ---
(90’) Every Watford pass is cheered as they keep the ball in Chelsea's half. There will be six minutes of stoppage time, however...
--- 89’ Substitution SUB! And that's Deulofeu's last action. Carrillo replaces the goalscorer. ---
--- 88’ Assist Doucoure's wonderful pass set Deulofeu away, with the Spaniard's speed simply too much for the Chelsea back line once again. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOAL! Deulofeu has been brilliant and he gets the goal he deserves! It's another individual strike, cutting inside from the right to shoot into the bottom-left corner, and that should be that. 3-1. ---
(86’) Back come Chelsea. Hazard is fouled on halfway. What a finish to this game.
--- 84’ Assist Pereyra teed up the shot, but it was all about Janmaat. What a magnificent goal. Watford are set for the three points once more. ---
--- 84’ Goal! GOAL! Janmaat! Incredible. The Dutchman scored a wonderful individual goal against Chelsea last season, but this is even better. He beats man after man, trades passes with Pereyra and then slides a reverse finish past Courtois. 2-1. ---
(84’) CHANCE! Deeney sets Deulofeu through and he almost restores the hosts' lead! The Spaniard's finish drops just wide of the far post. So close.
(83’) Watford head straight back up the other end and Zeegelaar hits the byline, his cross deflecting up kindly for the grateful Courtois.
--- 82’ Goal! GOAL! Brilliant from Hazard and Chelsea are level! The Watford players cannot believe it. The little Belgian beats Mariappa twice and then, from 25 yards, shoots into the bottom-right corner. It's a scarcely deserved equaliser but an equaliser all the same. 1-1. ---
(81’) SAVE! Fabregas draws a first save from Karnezis. It's lovely football from Chelsea, Hazard cutting the ball back for Azpilicueta to dummy. In came Fabregas with a low curler, but the Watford goalkeeper got down smartly.
(80’) SAVE! The Hornets do eventually get a shot off through Pereyra, but Courtois holds on.
(79’) Vital defensive work from Fabregas! Deulofeu has too much pace for his compatriot and squares to Doucoure in the area, but Fabregas gets back to smash clear as the Watford man readied a shot.
(78’) There are just a few nerves creeping in among the home supporters as Zeegelaar gives up a throw-in in his own half. Watford have dominated, but they still lead by just the one goal.
(77’) It is again Watford who push forward in search of getting the second goal. A high cross is claimed with ease by Courtois.
(75’) Chelsea are keeping the ball, but they have not tested Karnezis yet and we are heading into the final 15 minutes. That's a concern for Conte.
(73’) CHANCE! Deeney intercepts when Deulofeu looks certain to score! A low cross from the left is heading straight for the Spaniard when his captain steps in, eventually attempting to tee up his team-mate who, by then, has no angle to aim at.
(73’) Capoue is frustrated as he's pulled back for handball when he looked to have set up a break. The Chelsea free-kick comes to nothing.
(72’) Wasteful from Capoue. He brings the ball forward and, with options either side, drags a low shot a long way wide.
(71’) The visiting Chelsea fans are roaring their team forward, but Watford take a minute to regain their composure and keep the ball. They lead 1-0 against the 10 men.
(70’) The game has been very open, but it's just getting a little scrappy. Giroud's lay-off is poor, letting Deeney in, but the Watford man also concedes possession with a sloppy touch.
(68’) Giroud fouls Prodl from the set-piece, catching the defender with a stray arm, and Watford can regroup.
(68’) CLOSE! A winding Moses run results in a cross that is blocked, but a second cross seeks out Giroud and his header is deflected just over the bar for a corner.
(67’) The initial delivery is cleared and Holebas then takes too long to send in a second cross, allowing Kante to knock the ball away.
(66’) SAVE! Doucoure is dominating the midfield and he almost finds the net. Deeney lays the ball off for his team-mate to charge through and sting Courtois' palms with a firm drive. Corner.
--- 65’ Substitution SUB! There's a Watford change, too. The lively Richarlison makes way for Pereyra. ---
--- 64’ Substitution SUB! Pedro cannot continue and it's a Chelsea debut for Giroud! All of his four league goals this season have come from the bench. Can he dig the Blues out of a hole here? ---
(63’) Meanwhile, Pedro requires treatment. He hobbles off the pitch with the aid of a physio.
--- 62’ Yellow card YELLOW! Chelsea lost their discipline in an FA Cup clash with Norwich City last month and they look like they could well do again here. Fabregas is the latest player booked for a late tackle. ---
(62’) At the end of a long passage of play in which there were tackles flying in all over the pitch, Janmaat drags a tame effort well wide.
(60’) AND AGAIN! Now Richarlison nearly doubles Watford's lead. Deeney wins the ball back instantly from the goal-kick and the Brazilian fires a shot across Courtois and just wide.
(59’) CLOSE! The free-kick is cleared only as far as Deulofeu, who shoots narrowly wide. Courtois was stretching and may not have got there.
--- 58’ Yellow card YELLOW! This has not been the return to the team that David Luiz would have hoped for and he's booked for lashing out at Zeegelaar by the touchline. ---
(58’) There's all sorts of space in the midfield for yellow shirts to run into when Chelsea give up possession. Deulofeu easily beats the advancing Cahill, allowing Deeney to find Janmaat. In comes the cross, but Richarlison's header bounces across the face of goal.
(56’) A trio of Watford challenges on the flank cannot dispossess Kante, with Hazard then shaping a pass out to Moses on the right. The Nigerian crosses, but there's no-one in the middle to get on the end of a pretty poor delivery.
(55’) Karnezis knocks the free-kick long and both Zeegelaar and Moses return to the action. Watford are on top in this one.
(53’) Zeegelaar belatedly clambers up and he's now in discussion with the referee as his head is tended to. He may well be able to continue.
(52’) Moses is back on his feet, but Zeegelaar remains down. The stretcher is being called for, with the Watford man still lying on his side.
(51’) Great header, Zeegelaar! Zappacosta gets to the byline and crosses towards the back post and Moses, but the Watford man is up first and nods clear. He takes a whack in the process and both players require treatment as the free-kick goes the way of the home side.
--- 50’ Yellow card YELLOW! Prodl is booked for an earlier foul on Hazard when the ball finally goes out of play. ---
(50’) David Luiz crucially intercepts! Richarlison controls a pass inside the area, but the defender gets a toe in to knock the ball back to Courtois.
(49’) Brilliant from Richarlison. He beats three men in the middle of midfield and bursts into the Chelsea half. The pass to Deeney is a little slow, but Watford keep the ball.
(48’) Richarlison sets Zeegelaar away again, but the pass inside to Deeney is short. Although Richarlison cannot win the ball back, Watford keep the pressure on in a bid to force yet more Chelsea errors.
(47’) Chelsea are starting the second half on the front foot, but Watford have the numbers to force the ball back up the other end. Richarlison retains a threat on the break.
(46’) KICK-OFF: We are up and running once more at Vicarage Road.
So Chelsea have it all to do. We will bring you the second-half action shortly...
Meanwhile, Deeney's goal was his third of the season, all of which have been penalties against top six clubs. The Watford captain previously netted from the spot against Arsenal and Manchester United.
The Blues have also now matched Watford's league-high seasonal tally of four red cards with that Bakayoko dismissal. Only Grimsby Town can top Chelsea's seven in all competitions in English football.
The half-time scoreline does not make good reading for Chelsea, and they have lost their last six league matches when trailing at half-time.
Watford are good value for their half-time lead against the 10 men of Chelsea, Deeney having netted from the spot following a foul on Deulofeu. Bakayoko was sent off earlier on for the Blues for two bookable offences.
(45’) HALF-TIME: Watford 1 Chelsea 0
(45’) CHANCE! Pedro should do much better as he blazes over. Moses gets away from Zeegelaar and feeds the Spaniard, but he cannot keep his left-footed shot down from inside the area.
(45’) The corner does not clear the near post and instead ruffles the sidenetting. There will be two minutes of stoppage time.
(45’) Corner to Watford. It could be more. Deulofeu does really well to cross from the right, but no team-mate can direct the ball goalwards. A second centre is blocked and eventually Capoue shoots wide, via a deflection.
--- 45’ Yellow card YELLOW! Richarlison is late to a challenge on Pedro and goes into the book. ---
(44’) "You're getting sacked in the morning," sing the Watford fans to Conte. Chelsea are struggling to regain a foothold in the game.
--- 42’ Goal! GOAL! Deeney rifles beyond Courtois! The goalkeeper tried to read the penalty and stay central, but he was not close to saving a powerful strike. 1-0. ---
(41’) PENALTY! Courtois brings down Deulofeu! The Spaniard has been lively throughout and he nicks the ball beyond the goalkeeper and rides the challenge to win a Watford spot-kick. Deeney to take...
(40’) Richarlison sets Zeegelaar away down the left, but the cross is blocked. Watford knock the ball backwards and build again. Chelsea have all 10 men behind the ball when out of possession.
(39’) It's Chelsea's turn to keep the ball. This will come as some relief to Conte after a difficult period, but they are not really threatening to trouble Watford in attack. It might take a moment of inspiration from a Fabregas or a Hazard.
(37’) Chelsea comfortably clear and then Pedro wins a free-kick from Janmaat as Watford overplay the ball. The hosts have plenty of time to win this game against 10 men.
(36’) Watford keep the pressure on and Moses is required to make a fine defensive header to deny Richarlison at the far post. Holebas shapes up for a long throw again.
(35’) SAVE! A first save of note for Courtois, but he gathers Richarlison's effort easily. A shot from the left was well hit but too central to trouble the goalkeeper.
--- 34’ Substitution SUB! Willian is the victim of Bakayoko's red card, with the Brazilian making way for Fabregas. ---
(33’) Chelsea now opt for an alternative approach, moving the ball around leisurely in their own half. When they do move forward again, Hazard buys a foul. Still no Chelsea change.
(32’) Hazard, Kante and then Willian lead a counter up the centre of the pitch for Chelsea, but a pass wide to Moses slows the move and Watford get men back - as they have done well throughout this first half.
(31’) Can Watford take advantage now? As Chelsea ready a change - Conte seemingly looking to Fabregas - the hosts keep the ball on halfway.
--- 30’ Red card! RED! A horrible showing meets a premature end for Bakayoko. He is off. A poor first touch allows Richarlison to nip in and a rash challenge brings a second yellow card in quick succession. ---
(29’) Watford get men back so quickly, but Chelsea work the ball really well to Zappacosta on the left. Although Moses knocks the centre down for Pedro to shoot against the post, the Nigerian used his arm to control the ball and the whistle is blown.
(28’) Again the defender opts to go short, though, and his eventual cross is easily claimed by Courtois. Chelsea can break.
(27’) Courtois comes for this one and punches well. Watford have a throw-in on the left, with Holebas winding up to launch the ball back into the box.
(26’) And another corner. It's a poor Deulofeu delivery, reaching only the near post, but it looks to be heading on target until Bakayoko clears.
(26’) The free-kick is launched towards Prodl, who loses out but wins the corner...
--- 25’ Yellow card YELLOW! Bakayoko has been particularly poor and he fouls Capoue clumsily after giving the ball to the Watford man. That's a booking. ---
(24’) There are so many loose touches from the Chelsea midfielders, giving Watford chance after chance to take possession. There is no way through this time, though.
(23’) Deeney holds the ball up really well in the area, pinning David Luiz, but the Chelsea man soon has help and the Blues can clear. There might have been a shooting opportunity there.
(21’) There's another Watford player down. This time Deeney is holding his back after a challenge on the right-hand touchline. The Hornets get the free-kick.
(20’) Willian and Azpilicueta superbly work space on the right for the former to look inside to Kante. The Frenchman's attempted pass out to Zappacosta on the left is woeful, however, flying over his team-mate's head.
(19’) There's a short stoppage as Deulofeu recovers, having taken the ball in the face from Zappacosta's challenge.
(19’) BLOCK! Cahill makes a vital intervention to deny Richarlison. An awful, lazy Kante pass gifts the Brazilian an opening, shimmying past the first challenge and shooting hard and low. Cahill blocks brilliantly.
(18’) Watford go short with Holebas, who then attempts to beat a man and commits a foul. That was a bizarre decision, with Chelsea players nearby.
(17’) Deeney is winning every header in the middle, with Richarlison feeding off the front man. Another dash down the outside of Azpilicueta results in a corner.
(15’) Azpilicueta recovers well to slow Richarlison on the left. The Brazilian had got away from his marker, but the defender ensures a deflected cross to the far side of the area is the best that can be mustered.
(13’) Hazard is crowded out every time he receives possession, with three Watford players in close attendance on this occasion. The Belgian is hobbling, too.
(12’) CHANCE! And now a real opening at the other end for Willian. Moses' centre hits Holebas and drops for the Brazilian to smash at goal from around 10 yards out. He clears the crossbar, when Karnezis would have struggled to react.
(10’) CHANCE! What an opportunity for Deeney. The corner reaches the Watford captain completely unmarked at the back post, but his attempted volley is completely miscued and bobbles wide. He really should have scored.
(9’) And now a corner to Watford. The Hornets are well on top, Richarlison's deflected drive running behind.
(9’) CLOSE! Deulofeu almost nets the opener. The speedy forward runs at David Luiz from the right, but he's forced a little wide and lashes his finish into the sidenetting.
(8’) WIDE! Doucoure drags across the face of goal. That move started with Richarlison picking out Janmaat on the right, with the consequent cross cleared only as far as the Watford midfielder. From 20 yards, he could not find the target.
(7’) Capoue wins a free-kick on the left for Watford, a team-mate having brilliantly halted the roving Hazard. The hosts are working hard.
(6’) Watford have started brightly, with the game largely played in the Chelsea half. Javi Gracia will hope for more of the same.
(5’) Good defending, Cahill! Bakayoko plays a loose pass and Deulofeu's intercepting first touch looks to take him beyond the Chelsea defence. Cahill steps across the former Everton man, allowing Courtois to claim.
(4’) A cross from the right clears Richarlison's head, before Deeney gets on the end of a delivery from the opposite flank. Chelsea scramble clear, with referee Mike Dean content that there was no handball. There are penalty appeals from the home supporters, but nothing from the players.
(3’) A nervy moment for Courtois early on. Deulofeu brings the crowd to its feet by haring after the Chelsea goalkeeper, forcing a punt that gifts Watford a throw-in in a promising position on the right.
(2’) Kante seeks out Zappacosta with an optimistic switch from right to left, but the ball runs behind for a goal-kick, some way ahead of the wing-back.
(1’) The two sides trade long balls in the opening minute, Courtois eventually collecting as the ball drops into his area.
(1’) KICK-OFF: Watford get us up and running.
The teams are in the tunnel. We are just a few minutes away from kick-off at Vicarage Road.
Who will take the points from this one? We're about to find out...
So there is understandably a great deal of focus on floundering Chelsea, but the Hornets are also in dire need of a result. Watford have not scored in Javi Gracia's first two games in charge in all competitions and they are just three points clear of the relegation zone.
Javi Gracia added: "It is always difficult to play against teams like Chelsea. This will be demanding physically and tactically."
"[David Luiz] has to play and prove that he deserves to play," Conte told Sky.
And there are new signings on the bench for both sides - Ndong and Lukebakio for Watford, Emerson and Giroud for Chelsea.
Watford look to match their opponents' shape, bringing in Janmaat and Zeegelaar. Conte makes three changes after Wednesday's loss. David Luiz is back in the side for the first time since October, while Moses and Willian also come in.
Subs: Willy Caballero, Antonio Rudiger, Emerson, Danny Drinkwater, Cesc Fabregas, Callum Hudson-Odoi, Olivier Giroud.
Chelsea (3-4-2-1): Thibaut Courtois, Cesar Azpilicueta, David Luiz, Gary Cahill, Victor Moses, N'Golo Kante, Tiemoue Bakayoko, Davide Zappacosta, Willian, Pedro, Eden Hazard.
Subs: Daniel Bachmann, Joy Mukena, Didier Ndong, Roberto Pereyra, Dodi Lukebakio, Andre Carrillo, Andre Gray.
Watford (3-4-2-1): Orestis Karnezis, Adrian Mariappa, Sebastian Prodl, Jose Holebas, Daryl Janmaat, Etienne Capoue, Abdoulaye Doucoure, Marvin Zeegelaar, Gerard Deulofeu, Troy Deeney, Richarlison.
Let's get the team news...
It will be crucial for Chelsea to bounce back here from their shock midweek home defeat to Bournemouth, and Watford - winless since Boxing Day in the league - could provide the ideal opposition.
Champions Chelsea are a huge 19 points off the pace set by runaway leaders Manchester City this season, with the Blues' Champions League qualification hopes now in peril as Tottenham close in on Antonio Conte's men.
Hello and welcome to our live text commentary of the Premier League game between Watford and Chelsea at Vicarage Road!

What a win for Swansea! Bottom of the Premier League at the start of the game, the three points they've earned lift them out of the relegation zone - at least temporarily - and just three points off Watford in 10th! Narrow margins separate the bottom half of the table. Monreal's opener was cancelled out by a Clucas double and an Ayew strike, following a calamitous display from Arsenal at the back. It finishes 3-1 to Swansea here!
(90’) The referee blows the whistle for the last time, and Swansea have a famous victory!
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Clucas has made the difference tonight, and gets a warm reception as he leaves to be replaced by Routledge. ---
(90’) Mustafi pings a forward pass straight out for a goal kick. Awful ball. Sort of sums up Arsenal's night really.
(90’) MISS! Giroud almost pulls one back form close range, but he can't quite meet a deep cross at the near post and it flies wide! It doesn't look like there will be enough time left for Arsenal to salvage anything from this game now.
--- 88’ Substitution The hard-working Ayew is replaced by Bony for the last few minutes. ---
--- 86’ Goal! GOAL! Another comedy of errors at the back sees Swansea increase their deserved lead! Monreal's failed acrobatic clearance allows Ayew in behind to cross into the middle, and the defence make a mess of clearing, allowing Clucas to smash home his second of the night! It's now 3-1 to Swansea! ---
--- 83’ Substitution Dyer comes off for Carroll as Carvalhal tries to hold out for the last few minutes. ---
(83’) Arsenal pepper the Swansea box with crosses, but can't quite make the most of them as Swansea hang on.
(80’) Another great chance is spurned as Monreal's cross is cut out with Arsenal shirts aplenty in the middle.
(79’) CHANCE! Ramsey produces a lovely flick to release Mkhitaryan in the channel, and his fizzed, low cross flashes across the face of goal, but nobody is there to capitalise!
(77’) It looks like Giroud is playing up front alongside Lacazette, with Ozil and Mkhitaryan in support of them. That front four have a little under 15 minutes to salvage something for Arsenal here.
--- 76’ Substitution Giroud replaces Iwobi as he comes on to try and rescue something from this game. Could this be his last game in an Arsenal shirt? ---
--- 75’ Yellow card Frustration is setting in as Ozil becomes the third Arsenal man to pick up a yellow card. ---
(74’) CHANCE! What an opportunity for a debut goal for Mkhitaryan! He had a free header inside the box from Ozil's cross, but his header is caught by Fabianski and the offside flag is raised anyway.
(71’) MISS! What a miss! Dyer latched onto a loose clearance from Mustafi, before racing into the box and hammering a left-footed strike just off the base of the post and behind!
(70’) Cech makes a hash of the resulting free-kick, which is swung in to the back post with pace. The keeper gets caught underneath it, however, and palms it behind for a corner instead of catching.
--- 69’ Yellow card Bellerín follows Elneny into the book for Arsenal. The Gunners are getting frustrated here. ---
(67’) Arsenal's attempts to force their way through the middle with quick exchanges is proving largely fruitless - they look much more dangerous when working the ball wide. However, Lacazette isn't exactly an aerial presence in the box, so don't be surprised to see Giroud come on for the last 20 minutes.
(65’) That goal wasn't the ideal impact Arsene would have wanted when he brought Mkhitaryan on. The Armenian has gone out to the left flank, with Iwobi switching to the right in a 4-2-3-1.
--- 61’ Goal! GOAL! Swansea lead! What a ridiculous goal to concede. Monreal and Mustafi play the ball backwards to Cech, who has three men on him. He tries to pass it out, and it's straight to Ayew, who pokes in from close range! What a crazy goal! Swansea won't care though, they're 2-1 up! ---
--- 60’ Substitution Mkhitaryan comes on for his debut! He replaces Elneny, and will hope to inspire his side to victory here. ---
(60’) Bellerin tries to cross low, but it's cut out. He gets a second bit of the cherry though, and his ball to the back post is much better, and forces a corner.
(57’) CHANCE! Dyer drives well down the right and shows good skill to beat his man, before Cech comes out to claim his low cross.
(56’) SAVE! Swansea can't clear as Arsenal play some nice passing in and around the box, but Ozil's eventual shot is tame and Fabianski is relatively untested.
--- 54’ Yellow card Elneny gets a silly booking for handball, his arm came out and blocked Fer's attempted pass. ---
(53’) CHANCE! Bellerin whips in a wonderful cross, but Van der Hoorn gets to it just ahead of Lacazette and clears behind for a corner. Xhaka meets it, but can't direct his effort on target.
(51’) MISS! Clucas meets a cross with his head from just inside the box, but it bounces narrowly wide of the target. It never really looked like testing Cech.
(49’) Some neat interplay on the right breaks down as Clucas gets a foot in, but he can only clear to nobody and Cech recycles possession.
(47’) Arsenal's passing looks more purposeful at the start of this second half, although the tone is very much the same - Swansea have everyone back defending.
(46’) And Swansea kick off at the start of the second half!
Swansea will perhaps feel unlucky not to be ahead at half time, having had the better chances and looked far more threatening in this first half. However, having said that, Arsenal will feel very disappointed to have let their lead from Monreal's strike slip so quickly, conceding almost immediately to Clucas. It's 1-1 at half-time, and the Gunners will need to show far more in the second period if they are to win this game, while Swansea simply need to be more clinical in front of goal.
(45’) Swansea play it forward, but the referee blows his whistle for the end of the first half.
(44’) MISS! Ozil and Iwobi work the ball well on the left, before feeding Xhaka on the edge of the box, but the midfielder's first-time strike is wild and way over the top of the bar.
(42’) Olsson gives away a pointless foul, pushing Bellerin over on the right when the right-back had nowhere to go. The resulting free-kick looks dangerous, but Fabianski can claim eventually.
(40’) CHANCE! Fer nicks it in midfield and drives at the Arsenal defence. hey back off to the edge of the box, but his side-footed shot is tame and doesn't trouble Cech. More sloppy play from Arsenal though.
(38’) Arsenal knock the ball around in Swansea's half, but they will be more than happy to let the Gunners have it in front of them. Elneny then crosses straight out of play from the right.
--- 34’ Assist Mawson has looked threatening pushing out of the back three at times, and he showed good ball-playing ability there to pick Clucas out in the final third. ---
--- 34’ Goal! GOAL! Swansea equalise almost instantly! It's sloppy defending from Arsenal as Mawson slips Clucas in behind, and the midfielder tucks a left-footed shot in at the near post to restore parity! That's so poor from Arsenal - they can't have been ahead for more than 60 seconds! ---
--- 33’ Assist What a ball from Ozil, who is having a stellar season. He's stepped up to be Arsenal's best player this term. ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOAL! It's that man Monreal again!! Very much against the run of play, Ozil swings in an absolutely fantastic ball to the back post, where Monreal ghosts in to stab home! It's 1-0 Arsenal, and Swansea will be ruing their wasted opportunities. ---
(31’) CHANCE! Another swift Swansea counter sees Ayew scuff a long shot wide of the post from outside the box, when he had team-mates in good positions. Swansea have been the better side by far in this first half, but they've been wasteful in the final third.
(30’) SAVE! Fabianski is forced into a diving save at his near post as Iwobi wriggles free of his marker and unleashes a fierce left-footed strike! However, the former Arsenal stopper is equal to it and parries it behind for a corner.
(27’) CHANCE! Elneny is forced to put Van der Hoorn's cross from the right out for a corner, before Mawson then wins another as he curling strike is deflected behind! Swansea still looking threatening, but unable to convert their chances as of yet.

Arsenal scored four goals in the opening 22 minutes of their last Premier League game against Crystal Palace – nine of their previous 10 goals in the competition had come after half-time.
Arsenal's away form has been very poor this season, having won just three of their 12 Premier League away games so far. The last time they’d won as few on the road this far into a season was 2005-06, earning their fourth away win in their 15th game. However, the Gunners have won four of their last five Premier League away games against the Swans, losing the other in November 2014 (1-2).
It has been all change for Swansea in a managerial sense since reaching the top flight - Carvalhal will be the seventh different Swansea manager that Wenger has faced in the Premier League in just 14 meetings.
Furthermore, the Gunners have only lost one of their last 34 Premier League games against the side starting that day bottom of the table (W27 D6), losing 4-3 at Blackburn in 2011. They have also scored in all six of their away Premier League games against Swansea - only at West Brom (12) and Birmingham (7) do they have a better 100 per cent record.
However, the Swans have lost four of their last five Premier League meetings with Arsenal - winning the other - and have been beaten in the last three.
Carvalhal has steadied the ship at Swansea since taking over, having lost just once so far and remaining unbeaten in their last five games in all competitions. However, they start the evening bottom of the Premier League table despite a confidence-boosting 1-0 win over high-flying Liverpool in their last league game.
Visitors Arsenal have bounced back with successive wins over Crystal Palace and Chelsea after a run of poor form that saw them fail to win in five games in all competitions, and will look to succeed where Liverpool failed and make it three on the spin here.

Jack Wilshere and Danny Welbeck miss out through injury, however, as Arsene Wenger makes just two changes to the team that beat Chelsea 2-1 last time out to reach the EFL Cup final. Aaron Ramsey takes Wilshere's place in midfield, making his first start since returning from injury, while Petr Cech is restored in goal for David Ospina, who drops to the bench.
Henrikh Mkhitaryan is named in the Arsenal squad for the first time since joining from Manchester United, and could well make his debut tonight. Olivier Giroud is also included on the bench, despite speculation linking him with Chelsea amidst the impending arrival of Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

(26’) This is much better from Burnley, they are keeping Newcastle deep inside the own half and putting pressure high on the home side. Barnes is causing plenty of problems for the Newcastle defence.
(24’) GOAL DISALLOWED! Barnes runs away to celebrate what he believes to be the opening goal of the game, but the referee already has blown the whistle for offside. It was an excellent finish by Barnes, he comfortably slotted the ball underneath Darlow from close range, but he had just strayed offside after a chip over the top by Charlie Taylor.
(22’) Head-to-head: The two sides only other previous Premier League encounter at St James' Park ended in a 3-3 draw in January 2015. So far we haven't had too many chances for that many goals tonight.
(20’) That Newcastle chance seems to have livened up the game now as Burnley have their first attack of the game. Jóhann Berg Guðmundsson lifts a cross into the box which Karl Darlow claims just as Barnes crashes into him, looking to get on the end of that ball.
(17’) OFF THE POST! Kenedy with almost the perfect arrival here! The winger took a couple of touches to take it past his markers on the edge of the box, he then fires a powerful shot at goal, it takes a deflection off Kevin Long, before smashing against the post. The rebound appears to fall perfectly to Christian Atsu in penalty area, who was unmarked and onside, but he can't get his feet sorted quickly enough and his weak effort is fired straight at Nick Pope. By far the best chance of the game.
(15’) It is set to be a busy evening for all teams tonight with the transfer deadline looming, and the Magpies have had a few outgoings, with Jamie Sterry, Jack Colback and Rolando Aarons all departing St James' Park today.
(13’) STAT: Newcastle are winless in seven Premier League home games, losing five of them. It's their longest run without a victory in the competition since April 2009.
(11’) The game is lacking quality at the moment, a lot of sideways and backwards passes by both teams, not much pace to the game so far. Newcastle arguably looking the stronger side, with Burnley sitting deep and inviting the hosts to play the ball in front of them.
(8’) Slow start to the game so far, neither side really threatening to open the scoring with both teams enjoying possession in the middle of the pitch and not looking close to carving open a chance in the final third.
(6’) Despite their poor recent form, Burnley haven't been conceding many goals, but they are struggling to get the ball in the back of their opponents net, with Chris Wood currently out injured, so Ashley Barnes once again leads the line.
(4’) Newcastle are enjoying an early spell of possession here, they are passing the ball nicely around the pitch, with new signing Kenedy already getting on the ball down the left wing and looking to cause Burnley early problems. An early goal for the hosts will be vital tonight, especially to ease the nerves of the home crowd.
(2’) Burnley won October's reverse fixture 1-0, thanks to a Jeff Hendrick goal, and could complete a top-flight league double against Newcastle for the first time since 1960-61.
